subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a cross-channel Gateway receipt timestamp to agents, and if so what field name, metadata block, and timestamp format should become the stable contract?
rationale: Source inspection proves the field is missing, but the fix would add a durable agent-visible metadata and plugin SDK contract across channels, so automation should not choose the public API shape unilaterally.

options.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose a single field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` through the shared inbound context/envelope path and cover at least one direct and one durable receive path with tests.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Do not add agent-visible metadata; rely on Gateway/channel metrics, logs, or traces for latency attribution.

options.title: Leave it to channel plugins
options.body: Let plugins expose their own receipt timing when needed, accepting inconsistent names and weaker cross-channel comparability.

recommendation.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose a single field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` through the shared inbound context/envelope path and cover at least one direct and one durable receive path with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have adjacent inbound metadata prompt-boundary history and handled the prior timestamp metadata issue closure, making them the best available routing owner for the product/API choice.
